newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwandan commander says he sent troops into Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan commander says he sent troops into Zaire.

text.p: A Rwandan army commander said on Wednesday he sent a detachment of troops into Zaire on Tuesday in retaliation for Zairean firing into Rwanda.
Lieutenant-Colonel "Caesar" told reporters he sent "a good-sized force" into Zaire from the border town of Cyangugu after nightfall, adding that the troops had also returned during the night.
"After they hit our territory and injured and killed our people and hit civilians we were forced to retaliate," he said.
"We retaliated by two means," he added. "We fired at them with heavy machineguns and mortars and we sent in a force to destabilise them and to force them away from where they could affect us."
The lieutenant-colonel, who did not give his full name, gave no other details of the operation.

Earlier on Wednesday Rwandan strongman vice-president Paul Kagame told a news conference in the capital Kigali that Rwanda would be forced to respond to what he termed Zairean aggression but he made no mention of any Rwandan sortie into Zaire.
